mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of expected earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.5% in a month, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations that prompt market participants to demand higher real yields, causing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in out-of-sample tests (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and a decline in UNRATE over two consecutive months suggests strengthening labor market conditions without wage suppression, which increases consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market strengthening without wage inflation
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when the labor signal is present (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in INDPRO by more than 1% following a period of expansion signals supply-side weakness that reduces market liquidity and elevates risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during prior supply expansions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST increases by at least 5% in a month, it reflects growing industrial production momentum that boosts optimism about future orders, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative during such demand spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising UNRATE above 4% indicate tightening labor market conditions that raise the cost of capital, depressing expectations for corporate profits and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not show consistent negativity during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 of at least 3% over three months suggests weakening demand absorption in the economy, which reduces growth prospects and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when the signal is active (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls by more than 10% in a month, it indicates a sharp contraction in inventory valuations that raises uncertainty and triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during such inventory declines (p > 0.05).
